blocks.text: In order to provide the Zscaler Unified Vulnerability Management (UVM) service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article. For UVM, logs are defined as the configuration and transaction data collected for actions performed by users authorized by you who are acting within the UVM SaaS Application.

Zscaler retains the logs on a rolling period of up to 180 days during your subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.
For the UVM Remediation Copilot feature, prompts and responses are stored by Zscaler for 90 days as part of the session history. Remediation Copilot is not trained using any customer data.
For the Mapping Copilot feature, prompts and responses are stored by Zscaler for 90 days as part of the session history. Mapping Copilot is not trained using any customer data.
Logs are stored in the European Union or the United States.
